articles.text:
FORT Robotics Secures About $20 Million In New Funding Commitments Led By Tiger Global And Mark Cuban Companies
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
FORT Robotics Secures About $20 Million In New Funding Commitments Led By Tiger Global And Mark Cuban Companies
FORT Robotics, a Philadelphia-based provider of safety technology for autonomous machines and robotics systems, has secured approximately $20 million in additional financing commitments from existing investors, including Tiger Global and Mark Cuban Companies. The investment consists of approximately $10 million in financing led by Tiger Global, with participation from Mark Cuban Companies, expected to close during the week of the announcement, and an additional $10 million commitment from Tiger Global to a previously announced private investment in public equity (PIPE) financing.
The PIPE investment is expected to close in connection with FORT’s proposed business combination with Newbury Street II Acquisition Corp. (NASDAQ: NTWO), a publicly traded special purpose acquisition company.
Including previously announced PIPE investments, the latest commitments bring total committed PIPE capital associated with the proposed transaction to more than $50 million.
FORT plans to use the additional financing to expand its workforce, strengthen operating capacity, and support growing customer demand across industries adopting robotics and physical artificial intelligence.
The company develops safety and security infrastructure intended to help autonomous machines operate reliably in environments where they interact with people and other equipment.
Its technology is marketed as a Trust Layer for Physical AI, providing capabilities designed to improve machine safety, secure communications, and operational control.
FORT’s products are used across warehousing, manufacturing, construction, transportation, agriculture, mining, energy, defense, and other industrial applications.
The company reports that its technology has been deployed across more than 19,500 units serving over 600 customers worldwide.
Its customer base includes Agility Robotics, DoorDash, Cobot, Zoox, Textron, and Google DeepMind.
As businesses introduce more advanced autonomous machines into workplaces and other operating environments, FORT sees increasing demand for safety infrastructure that can be integrated across different robotics platforms.
The company focuses on helping manufacturers and end users improve safety, support certification requirements, and accelerate deployment of autonomous systems.
The new financing will support FORT’s efforts to serve expanding customer opportunities, particularly in warehousing, construction, defense, and other markets where robotic systems are being introduced at greater scale.
Tiger Global has invested in FORT since 2022, when it led the company’s Series B financing.
The latest commitment follows several business developments, including an expanded partnership with Agility Robotics and the introduction of FORT’s Connectivity Aggregation software product.
FORT was founded in 2018 and has secured 25 patents covering technologies associated with robotics safety and autonomous operations.
The company is pursuing a public listing through its proposed merger with Newbury Street II Acquisition Corp.
Upon completion, the combined business is expected to operate as FORT Robotics Holdings and trade on the Nasdaq Stock Market under the ticker symbol FROB, subject to applicable approvals.

articles.title: Michigan State University Receives $20 Million NSF Grant For Space And Semiconductor Research Facility
articles.snippet:
Michigan State University received a $20 million grant from the U.S. National Science Foundation to establish the Integrated Diamond and Carbon Research in Space Applications facility, or IDiCaRS, a shared-use research center focused on semiconductor technologies designed for extreme environments.
The post Michigan State University Receives $20 Million NSF Grant For Space And Semiconductor Research Facility appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Michigan State University Receives $20 Million NSF Grant For Space And Semiconductor Research Facility
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 14, 2026
Michigan State University Receives $20 Million NSF Grant For Space And Semiconductor Research Facility
Michigan State University received a $20 million grant from the U.S. National Science Foundation to establish the Integrated Diamond and Carbon Research in Space Applications facility, or IDiCaRS, a shared-use research center focused on semiconductor technologies designed for extreme environments.
The facility will bring together advanced diamond and carbon materials research, electronic device fabrication, and high-energy radiation testing to accelerate the development of electronics capable of operating in space and other harsh environments.
Space radiation can damage conventional semiconductor devices, presenting challenges for spacecraft operating beyond low Earth orbit and for future missions traveling farther into space.
IDiCaRS will create an end-to-end research infrastructure to develop diamond and related carbon materials, fabricate electronic devices, and test how those devices respond to radiation.
The facility will be led by Wen Li, MSU Research Foundation Distinguished Professor in the College of Engineering and executive director of Fraunhofer USA Center Midwest.
High-energy radiation testing will use heavy-ion beams at Michigan State University’s Facility for Rare Isotope Beams.
MSU described the project as a first-of-its-kind niche facility, including a diamond foundry intended to allow researchers to move more quickly from materials development through device fabrication and harsh-environment testing.
Diamond is considered promising for space electronics because of properties including high thermal conductivity and resistance to high temperatures, radiation, and electrical stress.
By combining capabilities that are currently distributed across different facilities and locations, IDiCaRS is intended to shorten development cycles and help establish shared testing and qualification approaches for electronics used in extreme environments.
The facility will leverage existing capabilities and partnerships involving the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams, the MSU Space Electronics Initiative, and Fraunhofer USA Center Midwest.
Research conducted through IDiCaRS could support development of more radiation-resistant and thermally capable semiconductors, potentially reducing spacecraft reliance on heavy shielding and redundant systems.
The technologies could enable smaller, lighter, and more efficient spacecraft systems while also contributing to high-power electronics and next-generation communications technologies on Earth.
IDiCaRS will operate as a shared-use resource for academic, industry, and government researchers.
Aerospace, defense, and satellite companies will be able to collaborate on radiation-hardened electronics for missions beyond low Earth orbit, while semiconductor and materials companies can access diamond growth, device fabrication, and radiation-testing capabilities.
Potential applications beyond space include power systems, electric vehicles, telecommunications, and other advanced electronics.
The project will also expand workforce development opportunities in Michigan.
Students will gain access to advanced semiconductor materials, manufacturing processes, research facilities, and specialized equipment.

articles.snippet:
Restate raised $20 million in Series A funding led by Singular, bringing the durable execution infrastructure company's total funding to $27 million. Redpoint Ventures and Capital One Ventures also participated in the round.
The post Restate Raises $20 Million Series A Led By Singular appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Restate Raises $20 Million Series A Led By Singular
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Restate Raises $20 Million Series A Led By Singular
Restate raised $20 million in Series A funding led by Singular, bringing the durable execution infrastructure company’s total funding to $27 million. Redpoint Ventures and Capital One Ventures also participated in the round.
Restate plans to use the financing for continued product development and expansion in the U.S., including the opening of a commercial hub in San Francisco.
The company was founded by members of the team behind Apache Flink.
Restate develops durable execution infrastructure designed to help distributed applications and AI agents recover from interruptions while preserving state and workflow progress.
The technology is already used by hundreds of companies.
Restate supports durable execution for Replit Agent and enterprise workflows at companies including DOSS and BILT Rewards.
The company’s architecture is based on a purpose-built distributed log and event-driven orchestrator that combines execution, state, and communication.
Restate does not require an external database or search system.
The company also recently introduced Bring Your Own Cloud, which allows customers to run managed Restate deployments within their own cloud accounts and virtual private clouds.
Restate said the approach is becoming increasingly important as AI agents run longer processes, call external tools, interact with other agents, and need to recover reliably from system failures.
KEY QUOTES:
“Durable execution solved an important problem: it made individual processes reliable. But software is increasingly made up of services, agents, workflows and state that all need to stay reliable as they interact.”
“We believe durability has to become a property of the infrastructure itself.”
Stephan Ewen, CEO and Co-Founder of Restate
“What excites us about Restate is that they are redefining where durable execution can be applied.”
Henri Tilloy, Partner at Singular

articles.title: AblePay Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By F-Prime
articles.snippet:
AblePay Health raised $20 million in Series A funding to expand its healthcare affordability and patient payment platform. F-Prime led the round, with participation from A1 Health Ventures and .406 Ventures.
The post AblePay Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By F-Prime appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
AblePay Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By F-Prime
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 8, 2026
AblePay Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By F-Prime
AblePay Health raised $20 million in Series A funding to expand its healthcare affordability and patient payment platform. F-Prime led the round, with participation from A1 Health Ventures and .406 Ventures.
AblePay plans to use the funding to accelerate growth, expand its technology platform, and reach additional healthcare systems and patients.
The company focuses on helping patients manage out-of-pocket medical expenses while improving payment performance for healthcare providers.
AblePay said Americans paid approximately $591 billion out of pocket for healthcare in 2025, representing a 6% increase from the prior year.
The company’s technology integrates with healthcare providers and provides guaranteed non-recourse payment on an accelerated and predictable timeline.
Patients receive flexible payment options and can potentially save on their out-of-pocket balances.
Members also receive access to an advocacy team that assists with billing questions and issues.
AblePay was founded in 2016 and is now entering its second decade of operations.
The new capital will support additional product development and expansion as the company seeks to address affordability challenges for both patients and healthcare organizations.
KEY QUOTES:
“Healthcare affordability affects both sides of the bill. Patients need a better way to manage the cost of care, and providers need a better way to collect the revenue they have already earned.”
John Fistner, Founder and CEO of AblePay Health
“AblePay has built a differentiated model that addresses a significant market pain point for both healthcare providers and patients. The company combines a compelling patient value proposition with meaningful financial and operational benefits for healthcare organizations.”
Nikhil Marathe, Principal at F-Prime

articles.title: Basalt Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By NEA
articles.snippet:
Basalt Health has raised $20 million in Series A funding led by returning investor NEA to expand its AI platform for post-acute care admissions. Existing investors Frist Cressey Ventures and 25m Health also participated. The round brings Basalt's total funding to approximately $24.5 million.
The post Basalt Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By NEA appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Basalt Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By NEA
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 4, 2026
Basalt Health Raises $20 Million Series A Led By NEA
Basalt Health has raised $20 million in Series A funding led by returning investor NEA to expand its AI platform for post-acute care admissions. Existing investors Frist Cressey Ventures and 25m Health also participated. The round brings Basalt’s total funding to approximately $24.5 million.
Basalt uses AI to process post-acute care referrals arriving through fax, portals or electronic medical record integrations and evaluate patients against a facility’s clinical criteria.
The platform also supports admissions, benefit verification and prior authorization workflows.
At Lifepoint Health, Basalt reduced median chart processing time by 86%, from 8.5 minutes to 1.2 minutes.
Basalt has worked with Lifepoint since its 2025 seed round and expects to expand to 49 additional Lifepoint markets by the end of 2026.
The company is also deploying across 62 ScionHealth hospitals by year-end, where the platform is expected to manage incoming referrals across a network of more than 6,000 practitioners.
Basalt plans to use the Series A proceeds to extend its platform from admissions into discharge and payer workflows.
The company will also expand its sales, marketing, implementation and engineering teams.
KEY QUOTES:
“Case managers are still sending 70-page packets and waiting for responses, while patients remain stranded in hospital beds. Basalt turns that uncertainty into fast, defensible decisions. This funding gives us the power to transform one of healthcare’s most stubbornly inefficient systems.”
Ben Hackett, Founder and CEO of Basalt Health
“Basalt is tackling a massive healthcare challenge with a rare combination of clinical impact, operational value, and rapid adoption. The company’s AI-powered platform is becoming essential infrastructure for care teams, and we’re thrilled to continue our partnership with Ben and the Basalt team to transform how patients move into post-acute care.”
Blake Wu, Partner at NEA and Basalt Health Board Member
“Basalt is what we mean when we say AI should disappear into the workflow. Case managers don’t see a chatbot. They see the right bed, faster, with a clear reason behind the decision. Ben and the team have done the hard work of making AI reliable on the documents healthcare actually runs on, and that’s why two major health systems are scaling it network-wide. We’re proud to have been part of the journey from the start.”
Merrill Anovick, General Partner at 25madison and Basalt Health Board Member
“Basalt represents the kind of innovation healthcare needs right now: technology that creates measurable value while fitting naturally into existing clinical and operational workflows. Their platform helps organizations identify opportunities sooner, streamline operations and patient access, and support better outcomes without increasing burden on frontline teams. We’re excited to see the company continue to scale its impact through this next phase of growth.”
Al Smith, Senior Vice President and Chief Information Officer of Lifepoint Health
“What started as a new technology platform with an innovation partner, has quickly transformed how our team members’ work every day. Basalt helps our teams work faster, make more informed decisions, and deliver a better experience for our patients and our partners.”
Sarah Stuart, SVP Growth and Transformation at ScionHealth

articles.snippet:
Kopin Corporation secured an additional $18.6 million sole-source award from the Office of the Secretary of War through U.S. Army Contracting Command under the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program.
The post Kopin Secures Additional $18.6 Million U.S. Army Award For Color MicroLED Technology appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Kopin Secures Additional $18.6 Million U.S. Army Award For Color MicroLED Technology
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Kopin Secures Additional $18.6 Million U.S. Army Award For Color MicroLED Technology
Kopin Corporation secured an additional $18.6 million sole-source award from the Office of the Secretary of War through U.S. Army Contracting Command under the Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program.
The new award brings Kopin’s cumulative IBAS funding to $34 million.
The funding represents the second major U.S. government investment supporting Kopin’s color MicroLED microdisplay technology.
Kopin plans to use the latest award to develop two additional MicroLED display configurations for ground-soldier and pilot applications.
The funding will also support expanding U.S.-based MicroLED manufacturing capabilities.
Kopin said the investment is intended to accelerate the onshoring of MicroLED manufacturing processes for advanced defense and commercial applications.
The company is developing the additional displays for next-generation soldier visual systems and pilot heads-up displays.
These applications require high brightness, rugged durability, power efficiency, and reliable performance across demanding operating environments.
Kopin said the technology could also support future weapon sights, helmet-mounted systems, and augmented reality platforms.
The award also advances Kopin’s broader strategy of supplying display and optical technologies across defense, medical, enterprise, and AI infrastructure markets.
KEY QUOTES:
“Securing additional IBAS funding represents significant continued validation of Kopin’s MicroLED technology and its importance to next-generation U.S. defense systems.”
Michael Murray, CEO of Kopin
“Combined with our previous IBAS investment, the U.S. government has now committed $34 million through IBAS to advance MicroLED technology.”
Michael Murray, CEO of Kopin
“This enables Kopin to accelerate the development and U.S.-based manufacturing of additional high-performance MicroLED displays designed for next-generation soldier and pilot systems while separately enabling the foundational MicroLED platform technology for our AI Interconnect products.”
Michael Murray, CEO of Kopin

articles.title: Atombeam Raises $18.3 Million, Bringing Total Funding Above $55 Million
articles.snippet:
Atombeam has raised $18.3 million through a Regulation A+ offering hosted on StartEngine, bringing the AI infrastructure company's total funding to more than $55 million.
The post Atombeam Raises $18.3 Million, Bringing Total Funding Above $55 Million appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Atombeam Raises $18.3 Million, Bringing Total Funding Above $55 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Atombeam Raises $18.3 Million, Bringing Total Funding Above $55 Million
Atombeam has raised $18.3 million through a Regulation A+ offering hosted on StartEngine, bringing the AI infrastructure company’s total funding to more than $55 million.
The company plans to use the capital to accelerate commercialization of Neurpac, its data compaction and encryption software, while advancing its Persistent Cognitive Machine, or PCM, through independent benchmarking and customer pilots. Atombeam said PCM completed its first full build in September.
Atombeam said its intellectual property portfolio includes 678 patent filings, with 308 issued or allowed and 370 pending. Neurpac is designed to reduce the volume of machine-generated data that must move across networks while allowing the original data to be restored at the receiving end.
According to the company, Neurpac can typically remove 50% to 90% of the data that needs to move in the use cases described in its announcement. Atombeam said the software can compact small packets that are difficult for conventional compression systems and increase effective bandwidth on infrastructure customers already own. The company cited deployments and validation across satellite, defense, and commercial communications.
Atombeam is separately developing PCM as an AI architecture with persistent memory and continuous learning capabilities. The company is targeting resource-constrained environments in which conventional large language models can be limited by computing, memory, power, or connectivity requirements.
Atombeam’s broader strategy combines AI-powered data infrastructure with a new model architecture designed for continuous learning. The company sees both technologies as responses to the growing network, data-center, and computing demands generated by connected devices and AI workloads.
KEY QUOTES:
“Closing this round marks an inflection point for Atombeam. We now have the capital, the team, and the technology to accelerate Neurpac adoption while bringing PCM through independent benchmarking and into customer pilots. Neurpac is in production with customers today, measured on their own traffic. PCM is something genuinely new: an AI that keeps learning after it ships and becomes an expert in the organization it serves with no data center behind it. In November we will put it beside conventional language models in independent benchmarks.”
“With Neurpac we are solving the challenges Large Language models exacerbate – wired, cellular and satellite networks and data centers pushed to the brink by heavy AI workloads and the barrage of data from connected machines. Simultaneously, with PCM we are creating a form of AI that addresses the very weaknesses of LLMs that lead to unprecedented network congestion and data centers that use as much power as small cities. In these ways we are using AI to address both the challenges of AI adoption today while creating the innovations required to realize AI’s full potential in the future.”
Charles Yeomans, Co-Founder, Chairman And CEO Of Atombeam
